findings.claim: The new dynamic probe list accepts every finite pixel minimum width but sends both the boundary and its following pixel to Chromium without respecting Chromium’s 10,000,000px emulation limit. An otherwise canonical completion with one harmless, ordered @media (min-width: 10000000px) rule that only changes body color is valid at ordinary browser widths, yet the public command reports 5 pass/2 fail: tasks 4 and 5 both throw when setViewportSize reaches 10,000,001px. The same control at 100000px and a harmless 1200.25px decimal rule pass 7/7. This is an edge-case false fail, separate from the now-fixed 800/1200 property-override false pass.
findings.recommendation: Bound dynamic rendered probes to Chromium’s representable viewport range, including the +1 probe, while retaining source-order validation for larger finite rules. Rules beyond that observable range that do not affect representable layouts should not crash otherwise correct work. Add passing harmless controls at the maximum boundary and above it, plus retained failing 800px/1200px override regressions.

items.note: Resolved for the accepted defect on the exact final bytes. The checker derives every supported finite authored minimum-width boundary and probes the boundary’s first matching integer viewport plus the following pixel. In the independent 11-valid/21-invalid matrix, the ordered 800px three-column override failed task 4 at 800px and the ordered 1200px block override failed task 5 at 1200px; redundant 800px and 1200px controls passed. Chromium independently confirmed the first divergence and required persistence through 1300px. A separate extreme emulation-limit false fail is recorded as a new low finding rather than reopening this false-pass finding.

Resolved on the exact final bytes. Both narrow preprocessing paths replace each comment with whitespace, preserving the lexical separation in @media/**/screen. The comment-separated route and @media/**/(...) control passed 7/7 and rendered the required layouts through 1300px; literal @mediascreen remained rejected 4/3 and Chromium kept its wider rules inactive.
